title: Using IRT Item Fit to Identify Poor-Quality Safety Benchmark Items

original_idea.body:
# Using IRT Item Fit to Identify Poor-Quality Safety Benchmark Items

**Problem:** Apply IRT to AI safety benchmarks

**Direction:** Fit a 2PL IRT model to a safety benchmark response matrix, then compute item fit statistics (S-X2, RMSEA, infit/outfit mean-square statistics) to flag misfitting items. Characterize what misfitting items look like: are they too easy (all models refuse), too ambiguous (refusal rates near 50%), or thematically confounded? Produce a ranked list of items by fit quality and suggest which items should be revised or removed.

**Why it matters:** Many safety benchmarks were constructed without psychometric item analysis. Poor items—those that are universally refused, that measure something different from the rest, or that are inconsistently responded to—add noise without adding information. IRT item fit statistics offer a principled, quantitative way to identify and remove such items.

**Relevant context:** 'Lost in Benchmarks' (2025) notes that benchmarks suffer from 'item saturation' (all models get them right) and argues IRT can identify this. The FairDIF paper (2025) applies IRT-based diagnostics to fairness problems. IRT item fit via mirt is well-documented and feasible in R without heavy coding.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain: poor-quality items add noise to safety evaluation, reducing measurement validity. Flagging misfitting items improves benchmark quality. The chain names the risk mechanism but the gap is that item removal requires benchmark maintainer adoption.

low_compute.reasoning: IRT model fitting and item fit statistics in R. Minimal compute, CPU-only.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Running item fit statistics in mirt is well-documented. Interpreting S-X2, infit/outfit and characterizing misfit patterns requires intermediate psychometric knowledge.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: fit IRT to one benchmark, compute item fit, rank and characterize misfitting items. A single focused analysis with a ranked list as output.

quick_reasoning: Directly addresses safety benchmark item quality with concrete IRT fit statistics; safety relevance is immediate for improving measurement validity.
